Had to rebuy this game on steam because EA deleted spore from my origin account for some reason
I contacted help at least 3 times over a year and never connected problem was never resolved.

Spore good

EA bad
A classic that DESPERATELY needs a spiritual successor since EA is allergic to making good games nowadays.

There is no other. 10 years later and you still can't find another game quite like this one. It's a shame really. Spore could have been the buggy, cringey, random grandparent of a whole new era of games that combine aspects of God Games, RTS, creature creators, RPG Makers, and civilization simulators. Limited? Yes. Repetetive? Yes. Buggy? Yes. Ugly? Definitely. But all of this doesn't sully the incredible ambition of Spore. There are plenty of games that let you explore a universe, trade, and make war as a preselected alien species. But there are none that allow you to develop a species from scratch. The Adventure Creator in the Galactic Adventures expansion is a criminally underrated gamemaking tool from a time before the Steam Workshop and Modding communities. Someday, someone will rediscover the stupendous potential of Spore, pick up what Maxis and EA crapped out, and develop an amazing follow-up to the genre.
Make horrific creatures and commit mass genocide. My kind of game.

I wish everyone a merry Christmas, but that´s not the full purpose of this review.

I discovered SPORE in 2012, more than 4 years ago and I can still enjoy it like I did then. This game isn´t only one of my all-time favourites, but my secondly most played game of all time as well. As you can see on my playtime, SPORE is absolutely massive and I don´t regret any minute I spent on it, not even those 2,880+ I had already collected on Origin. I am thankful this is now also available on Steam, but unfortunately EA games are simply not made to be here, EA doesn´t give a **** to their Steam-community.

Whom do I recommend SPORE to? 
(All following aspects are listed in order of importance)

Explorers: First spot, definately. If you love to spend your time on uncovering secrets, this game is perfect. Especially the last stage has tons of things waiting to be discovered by YOU. If you aren´t an explorer, don´t be afraid, this one is OPTIONAL, you can "complete" SPORE without finding all secrets as well.

Creative: Very close to the previous type. The designers feature nearly INFINITE possibilities. There´s almost nothing you can´t create, your imagination is the only limit. More than 400 Creature-, 500 Vehicle- and 600 Building-parts to use, modifacation of those and no set placements allow an unbelievable ammount of possible combinations. In fact there is no object looking like another one.

"God-wannabes": Write your own story from the very beginning. Start as nothing but a little cell, the most simple lifeform, evolve to an intelligent group leader and rise to the lord af the largest empire in the entire universe. 

Mess-Around: Everything said. Build ugly monsters and use them to kill everybody, edit the surface of planets, transform water into lava, highjack your friends, wipe out innocent creatures... The only limit is your free time :D

Challengers: Who said this game was going to be easy to finish? In fact it´s impossible, the last stage is endless... And trust me, if there´s one thing you have to try to understand, it´s (Spoilers Ahead) reaching the galactic core and wiping out the Grox... I wish you fun at exterminating around 2000 star systems...

Children: I know this has a teen-rating, but seriously, nobody would be mad about a six-year old playing this. Of course you can literally take out the entire universe without showing mercy, but the brutality is way to low to be frightening to anyone... Come on, the animation isn´t even realistic...

Non-EA-haters: I am afraid, but that´s the point I have to admit. The only thing I dislike this game for, but only the Steam version. EA doesn´t let Steam-users connect to their servers, so all online-features are disables for us. Bad thing that you can´t share your creatures or download other´s epic content, but this review won´t change either. EA isn´t ready for Steam yet and won´t ever be. I think singleplayer fun can annihulate this point, but the condition is bad, that´s sure.

Do I recommend Spore to anyone else? 


I am not sure about this one, to be honest. This might be considered too kid-friendly for some adults and too boring for action-gamers. 

This review is intended to be funny, just as SPORE is. In fact I want to say that you shouldn´t miss this, SPORE is just a game everyone should at least know. Please, get it in a sale. I do not force you to play this for as long as I did. Since there are no achievements you can also get rid of this within a daytime. I am still really surprised by this, SPORE just marked the simulator-genre, it´s still the one and only god simulator. I know there aren´t even many, but those few won´t ever reach this. 

Why do I say "get it in a sale" when it seems like I am amazed enough to pay it fully?

Because I didn´t either. Spore without online support isn´t just worth it. Get the Origin version if you don´t mind. saving your progress for this is important and sharing creations keeps the community alive. SPORE is an amazing game, but the publisher isn´t a great one.

Keep it up, guys ;)

Spore is one of those games that tried to reach the stars, failed in that and was justly criticized for being quite mediocre in many points of gameplay. And it was not like "hey, we've tried to build a moon lift, but managed only a third of it". A third of a moon lift would be totally meaningless in terms of resources consumed but at the same time a very magnificent instalment. Spore case is different.

It's closer to the idea of baking pizza from several hundreds of ingredients that, surprisingly, not collide together all that well. And yeah, theoretically, we have a working solution: we just need to roll the dough for some meters in length. But we don't have an appropriate oven to bake it all, so we cut our job in five stages, planning to build them all together after the oven stage. And that's where it all fails. Especially when your oven is running on electricity, and someone cuts you off the grid when you're not complete with baking all the pieces.

Spore is much under-developed. It divides into 5 different fragments, with drastically different gameplay between those parts, and the good half of the game is seriously underbaked, while the biggest, the final stage, when your species finally reach the space, is so big, so rich with particles, and so empty in terms of connected, entertaining gameplay, that it makes the stars blow out from impatience, from overly long expectations, from the ridiculous grind, from the absence of at least some sort of order...

And yet Spore is still a great game. My kids enjoy playing it, hours after hours. They rarely make it to the 4th stage, the civilization, let alone the 5th, that Space Void that is so big and depressing. But the first and second stages, where Spore is not an underdeveloped strategy game yet, but a good action-RPG with so rich options to build your character, while observing or participating all these events that are possible in such a giant sandbox, which this game is... That's really cool!

Sure, the game lacks achievements, lacks certain goals on all stages. Even more, it lacks the proper development on the 3rd, tribal stage, with at least as many options as we had on the 2nd (preferably more). It lacks some better control options and scope of events on the 4th stage. And it certainly lacks some glue, some intermediate stimulus to run through space on the final 5th stage. Oh, and maybe better tutorials and languages support for a younger audience.

All in all, despite all the misfortunes of the Spore development, production, the disastrous politics of the publisher which almost sunk Spore under the pile of excrements... It is a very good sandbox game. Where you build your character from a single cell into the reasonable creature, which makes its way up the evolution ladder all the distance to the stars and what beyond.

My mark is 7/10, I certainly recommend it for kids above 4-5 years old. Many players might find this sandbox both over- and underwhelming, due to its inconsistency. But hey, it's a unique title. One of a kind. And it is more than able to provide some delight with its gameplay, despite all weak spots. You just need an open mind to catch it.

When I installed Spore on my PC I expected a science toy in the guise of a game. Create a cell. Guide it toward civilization. Watch it march into the stars. What I didn’t expect was how quickly it would metastasize into the architecture of my daily life

The cell stage taught me hunger before it taught me joy. I scavenged. Devoured. Fled. Then I noticed myself doing the same in my career. Always scrabbling for nutrients. Never stopping to ask if I was full? The creature stage was worse. I sculpted abominations with too many eyes. Not enough balance. Then realized I was sculpting myself the same way. Clumsy. Overburdened. Desperate to appear fit for survival

By the time I reached the space stage I was no longer playing a game. I was playing a thesis. Everything we call society is just an ecosystem of temporary mutations. One step away from collapse if we stop adapting. That realization has not left me. It stares at me from the edges of every headline. Every election. Every whispered debate about democracy’s future

The disturbing thing is how Spore hints. Accidentally maybe. That if we remembered we were all once cells drifting in the same broth. Our systems of governance might hold. Cooperation isn’t lofty. It is primal. To ignore it is to de evolve

I live differently now because of this game. I eat differently. I argue differently. I dream differently. My loved ones with strange appendages. My city mutating overnight. My own hands reshaped into tools. It is not comfortable. It is clarifying

Why is Spore not more widely cherished. It is imperfect yes. But if we allowed its lessons to spread like spores in a damp forest. Maybe the world would be a better place. Stranger. Freer. Perhaps still democratic

Spore. It's a great game, seeing as it has been effectively discontinued. It has a decent daily player count, and an already expansive list of community creations. It has a few mixed genres, so something for everyone.

It all starts in the cell stage, a top-down arcade style section. This is the beginning of the impact your creature has on the galaxy. A simple stage, in 2D with 3D graphics, and, in my eyes, acts as more of a prologue to the rest of the game. All decisions you make in this and subsequent stages affect abilities you unlock in future stages.

Then, we move toward the creature stage. This stage moves the game to an RPG. It moves the environment into 3D, and gets your creature to its final evolutionary form. This is where it gets more complex. I would recommend spending a decent amount of time in this stage to gather as many parts as possible, because once you enter the next stage, you cannot change how your species looks.

After the creature stage, comes the tribal stage. This one functions more like a real-time strategy section. You are either pitted against or made to befriend other species who have arisen into tribes. I personally struggled with this stage, until I figured out how to equip the tools I had bought. That felt embarrassing. You can also customise your tribesmen in this stage, but only their outfits.

Next, we move to the Civilisation stage. This stage just moves down to strategy. Rather than more vicious, mixed, or social routes, you are given the choice of focusing on military, economy, or religion. You are now introduced to the currency you will use for the rest of the game. After taking over all the cities, your species now can travel to space.

Finally, the space stage. Some would argue this is where the game truly begins. All paths you took designate you a philosophy, and abilities to go along with it. You can now explore the whole galaxy, and find out about the galactic core and the grox. Your savegames can interact to some extent in this stage, and they can form alliances. Other species also grow into space, and you can ally, attack, and trade with them. This is the endgame stage. The finale to the journey of spore. Complete missions for your empire and others, and find out the secrets in the galactic core, guarded by the grox...

To conclude, it is an amazing game. Definitely worth buying.

A majority of my playtime is in Spore: Galactic Adventures. This is a review for after 2020.

This game is extremely interesting. It's one of those games that always captured my childhood attention. I never got to play Spore when it was released; I played it more than a decade later.

Cell stage: You start out the game as a cell; eating things to grow to bigger sizes. This is really just an intro piece of gameplay.

Creature stage: I played in this stage way more than I should have. I wanted to create the ULTIMATE MASTER CREATURE TO BEFRIEND OR DESTROY THEM ALL. I do believe this strategy helped me out in the long run. This area of the game has minimal gameplay. More than the cell stage, but there is a lot to be desired here. I really enjoy the creatures and world of this game however.

Tribal stage: This is another transition stage. It does some cool stuff and has some interesting mechanics. I don't believe a lot that you do here has an MAJOR effects on the future, unless you get killed. My first play ever, in creature stage, I was a carnivore and killed everyone. Several tribes aligned against me when I reached this stage and they destroyed me. That was cool, but I chose to start over to be friendlier.

Civilization stage: This is a lot like tribal stage but you get some vroom vroom bois and some water speedsters and some whooooooosh crafts. 

Galactic stage: Alright, FINALLY, you have made it to space. This is where the real meat of the game lies. I enjoyed this portion of the game the most. It adds like 10 times the amount of gameplay options and stuff to do. The scale and things you can do in this game is pretty mind blowing for an older game like this. This is the No Man's Sky of the past. The things that killed the game for me is I play on a 4k TV. The UI is just too small. I could play on a lower resolution, or a smaller monitor, but I'll just move to No Man's Sky instead of spending 100's of hours in this game.

TO CONCLUDE: Spend time getting the most resources in creature stage to have a powerful creature. Space stage is the best, has lots to offer, has really cool mechanics I don't know many games having, and is very impressive for the age of this game. There is some UI and interface issues playing on modern equipment.

Spore: A beautiful, untimely video game that perfectly manifests an ethics of becoming --- that is to say, playing spore is to become worthy of one's fate. Allow me to explain. In the game of Spore, the player begins as an amorphous space goo with no meaningful characteristics. As the player progresses, they choose defining traits according to their play style and fate. How does one build their creature? With love, and compassion for the animal; but also with a sense of purpose. Spore encourages the player to choose adaptations with a mind towards the function of the appendage. For example, one may choose to modify the mouth of the creature for better biting. As the creature slowly develops through this process of evolution, they begin to manifest the decisions they made earlier in the game --- they become worthy of their fate. At the beginning of the game, it is not at all clear why the space blob decides to spare or destroy other creatures. This is the creature in its least ethically developed stage. As the creature progresses however, what it ought to do becomes obvious through its body. Should a creature spare or destroy another creature? Well, does it have level 4 bite, or dance? In this regard, the decisions that the player ought to make in the interest of their own power and duration become obvious as the game progresses. 

The end of spore is a tragedy. It is the return to radical potential or possibility. In some sense, the last creature-man, the final form, is the closest to space goo of all the stages. At the end of the game is pointless, decadent, and filthy colonization and a desperate search through empty space for some kind of meaning, for anything at all. It comes in cryptic pieces of past civilizations and distant concurrent ones. The creature at the end of the game is lost and confused, a far cry from the one fighting for survival in Creature Mode or Tribal Mode. Even compared to Civilization Mode, the Space Mode creature's predominant new feature is despondent confusion. 

This was the first video game I ever played at five years old. My father was gifted a hard copy when I was two or three, when it came out. I played it on a shitty, slow computer in my parents bedroom mostly by myself. On and off through my early childhood and teenage years I played this game, coming back to it after months or years of intermittently forgetting about it. Now, as a young adult, I've come back to this game. I purchased it for myself to play on my computer at college. This is one of the only games I've played that has simultaneously astonished me and allowed me to inject my imagination into it. This game is about creativity and its about history. So much of my history is wrapped up in it; but furthermore, the game invites you to experience history itself, by giving the player a multi-generational perspective that is nonetheless deeply emotionally invested. I said earlier that the game is untimely: what I meant by that is not that its eternal or that it doesn't feel dated, but that every time I play this game, it speaks to my current condition. The message of this game has not been trivialized by cliche or irrelevance --- it is a classic bildungsroman. 

I doubt this review will encourage anyone on the fence to purchase this game. After all, the game is over ten years old, and my perspective on the game is deeply personal. However, I hope that this review will perhaps be seen by other fans of Spore, and provide them with a well-deserved affirmation that this game is a modern masterpiece.

This game is still one of the most incredible games I've ever played. There is just so much content and replay value that I've lost hours and hours of free time playing it. You start as a simple, microscopic cell that can only really eat food and attack things, and evolve through Creature stage, which is essentially where all the species surface onto dry land and form nests and packs, through to tribal and civilization stages, and finally Space stage.

Space stage is absolutely incredible, with not just a single explorable solar system, but a single explorable galaxy. The scale is incredible, with every single star having its own planet system. Some planets are in the tribal stage, some in creature, some in civilization and some in space. The game is truly incredible. 10/10

This game is providing me with what I have always dreamed of. ABSOLUTE POWER OVER THE ENTIRE GALAXY! if I play my cards right. 
Every stage of this game is good fun. I abolutely love this game.

My only complaint is that in the final stage of the game your empire becomes soo large that personally dealing with every little thing and trying to handle the spice trading for your entire empire with your one player controlled ship really started sucking. I wanted to be able to Age of Empires style delagate responsibilities to computer controlled characters. like trading, like military action, like colonization. I wanted to end up being the emperor who could just watch the empire I had built continue to grow, and spread, and take everything over everything. After the setup and planning you do in the first stages of the game, only require minimal player interaction, which would leave me (the emperor) the freedom to go do whatever I wanted. (like finding galactic adventures and lvling my captain. that was fun.) 

That said, this game is fun and totally worth the cost. Its just not made to allow you to be able take over the galaxy to the scale that I had wanted, in other words its sort of soft-capped out. There comes a point when you reach a size where you simply cannot manage everything personally, and you start losing planets as fast as you are gaining them.

This game is one of the most immersive games I've ever played. Not because of seamless gameplay or impeccable graphics, but for how it makes you care what happens to your creation. I've been playing for a long time over many different accounts and phases of my life, but every time I make a new world and see that weird looking rock hit my new planet, it feels like a new adventure. A great game for all ages!

Spore is a great game, but if you buy it on steam your game no longer comes with a CD key. This means you cannot register your game, and not being able to register your game means you cannot use online features. 
The online features include sharing creations with friends, downloading others creations, and being able to theme your save files as "my creations."

If you want online features go buy it on EA. I had to buy it twice. I spent hours going over guides to figure out work arounds that previously worked, and all of them were dead ends. 

For this reason alone I can't recommend you buy this game on Steam.

The actual game: 
It came out in 2008 and somehow had modern resolution support which was a pleasant surprise. 
It was great to make my own little cell and decide if it wanted to be vicious or friendly to any other creature it met. 
The creature creator is super fun to play with, and there are tons of hidden extra ways to modify your creations in complex ways.
(Alt-copy, ctrl-break apart limbs, A- asymmetry mode, tab-refined rotation tool)
The tribal stage is the first stage you really start to feel repercussions for if you were being aggressive. 
The civilation stage is so quick and easy as an economic nation, and so very, very hard as a military nation. 
The space stage is giant and mysterious, and you can spend 95% of your time just exploring and colonizing planets. 

It's a great game, and seeing *my* creations while exploring planets really mattered to me. I don't really care about spreading more maxis "Hoosie" creatures while I terrestrialize planets. 

I love this game, but rethink buying it here. I did hear it also has the same problem on Good old Games.

If ever there was a game that divided opinion, Spore is it! While i can see why it frustrated a lot of people by taking the relatively cutesy path rather than being a genuine look into genetically creating different creatures, it still gives you a huge amount of options when it comes to making your own creations. The second level is where you really get to flex your creativity and is without doubt the best level in the game. It does rather tail off as you get further into it, especially the fifth stage (space travel), but when you feel like a break from the missions themselves, you can simply head back into the creature creation section and create an entire planet's worth of creatures. If you should find this at a sale price, i would recommend it then, but at full price... maybe not.
